what: the Color 4 remainder — hwb, the Lab families, color() and the system colours — lands on Chrome's bytes
note: `test: null` — the whole suite. Every expected byte in
raster_colour4_test.dart is a Chrome measurement, so a mutant that
survives it has by definition stopped matching the browser somewhere the
The ticket's three named mutations — a hue direction, a matrix element,
a clamp — are all here, plus the traps this implementation specifically
invites: the derived-matrix construction (one primary digit feeds every
space that shares the white point), the modern-comma refusal, and the one
system colour whose alpha is not 255.
The Bradford element case mutates the 3x3 that both `lab()` and
`prophoto-rgb`/`xyz-d50` adapt through, so it proves the adaptation is
shared rather than duplicated — a second copy would let one path go red
Two first-run survivors were re-judged rather than kept (#34's rule): a
third-decimal Bradford drift moves no measured byte through rounding, so
it became a realistic digit swap; and the linear-space clamp turned out
to be a second copy of the byte clamp behind a monotone transfer, so the
copy was deleted (#40) and the case now targets the one clip that exists.
